title: What Next Generation 911 Can Do That Old 911 Can't #shorts
summary: Next Generation 911 is an internet-based system that can carry photos, video and texts; phones already blend satellites, Wi-Fi and sensors to locate a caller.
sources: Wireless 911 calls have historically been routed by the location of the cell tower that handles the call; ATIS estimates that on average 12% of wireless legacy E911 voice calls are misrouted; location-based routing is required when the caller's location is known within 165 meters at 90% confidence (nationwide carriers within 6 months, rules effective 13 May 2024); device-based hybrid location uses crowd-sourced Wi-Fi, A-GNSS and other handset sensors (FCC Report and Order, Location-Based Routing for Wireless 911 Calls, Federal Register, 13 Mar 2024): https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2024-03-13/html/2024-03157.htm

NG911 is a digital, internet protocol (IP)-based system that will replace the analog 911 infrastructure; it allows voice, photos, videos and text messages to flow from the public to the 911 network (911.gov, Next Generation 911): https://www.911.gov/issues/ng911

scenes.narration: {911|Nine one one} is moving onto internet technology. Next Generation {911|nine one one} can carry photos, video and texts.
And phones already help find you, blending satellites, nearby Wi-Fi, and their own sensors.
So the next {911|nine one one} won't just hear you. It can see what you send.
